questions.prompt: Which of the following is not one of the stages of faith?
options: Having an Islamic name.
Confessing by tongue.
Having enough knowledge about it.
Practicing what we believe in.
questions.note: A name alone does not establish inward belief or conduct. The knowledge/acknowledgment/action formulation appears in Nahjul Balagha saying 227; compare practical remembrance in the review.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is true?
options: Any Muslim is faithful, but not vice versa.
Any faithful person is a Muslim, but not vice versa.
There is no relationship between faith and Islam.
Faith comes first and then Islam.
questions.note: Within this course’s technical distinction, inward iman is more than outward profession of Islam; Quran 49:14 illustrates the distinction. This is not permission to pronounce judgment on an individual’s sincerity or to deny moral worth to other people.

questions.prompt: A person finds a good habit or attribute in a friend and says “I wish I also had it.”
options: This is jealousy and is bad.
It is not jealousy and is not bad.
This is jealousy but exceptionally is not bad.
None of them.
questions.note: The intended distinction is constructive emulation without wishing the other person to lose the good quality, versus destructive envy. The stem states no wish to deprive the friend. Compare the review’s envy obstacle; this is not the same as coveting another’s loss.

options: Talking about a wrong habit which exists in a person.
Talking about a wrong habit which does not exist in a person.
The same as accusation.
Exactly the same as insulting a person.
questions.note: A is closest among these choices, but is an incomplete definition: the relevant truthful disclosure is something the absent person would dislike. False attribution is slander. Necessary advice or reporting harm must not be conflated with malicious gossip.
evidence: Primary definition of backbiting and slander: https://sunnah.com/muslim:2589

questions.prompt: What does the Quran say about mocking others?
options: If it is normal and a little, it is allowed.
Do not mock others because they may be better than you.
Mocking people of other nationalities has no problem.
None of them.
questions.note: Quran 49:11 explicitly gives the possibility that the ridiculed people are better than those ridiculing them. Nationality is not a license for humiliation.

questions.prompt: The source quotes: “When a believer dies and leaves behind a paper on which there is knowledge ...”. What does this saying indicate?
options: The importance of teaching and writing.
The importance of doing research.
When someone dies, they should leave a will.
Before we die, we should clear our debts.
questions.note: The photographed mark is B (research), while A is the most direct reading of a written legacy that transmits knowledge. The notes p. 6 connect teaching with writing by the pen; the fragment does not specify how that knowledge was obtained. Both A and the supplied broader research interpretation B are accepted for this imprecise item. The incomplete saying is not presented as an independently authenticated complete hadith.
